title: New York becomes first state to pause hyperscale data center permits
key_facts: Governor Kathy Hochul, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Pat Ryan toured Fishkill Farms in East Fishkill, Dutchess County and held a roundtable with farmers, advocates and businesses.
The topic was the impact of hyperscale data centers, including a proposal in East Fishkill.
This summer Hochul signed an executive order pausing new hyperscale data center development.
It pauses discretionary state environmental permits for up to one year while a regulatory framework is built.
Hochul called it a 'nation-leading data center moratorium'; Ocasio-Cortez said it was signed in July.
quote_evidence: This action has temporarily paused discretionary State environmental permits for up to one year in order to build a regulatory framework that will protect ratepayers, the environment, the energy grid and communities across the state.
In July, Governor Hochul took action to protect farmers and working New Yorkers by instituting a one-year moratorium on data center construction.
why_it_matters_hint: A temporary state pause is meant to give time to write protective rules.
notes: Order dated by Ocasio-Cortez's quote only to July; day not stated. Text reads like a governor's office release.
